testing_gaps: CollaborationApiIntegrationTest covers sequential revocation and same-second rebinding, but not concurrent unbind with publication or acknowledge/close. The new relation, notification and event locking interactions therefore lack real-MySQL concurrency coverage for the immediate-revocation contract.
The MySQL fixtures use a single test transaction and do not cover simultaneous independent queueAbnormalEvent calls or cross-transaction deduplication.
No supplied frontend test covers navigation or filter changes during pending requests, where generation guards must prevent stale authorization data from reappearing.

Expiry fanout concurrent with unbind and same-second rebind needs independent-transaction MySQL verification. Existing rebind coverage is sequential within one test transaction; whether UPDATE JOIN/gap/event locks prevent stale family notification insertion after cancellation remains unresolved. No failing interleaving was established.
The transactional MySQL integration tests and mocked dispatcher tests do not exercise a real publication rollback followed by failure bookkeeping in a separate committed transaction.
